paragraphs.notes: Continuation page of the Patentansprueche. The page carries no claim number and no paragraph marker: it is one unbroken run-on enumeration of substituent group names that begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence with a trailing comma. It continues the sentence broken at the foot of printed page 85 (PDF p87), which ends '... Amino, gegebenenfalls substituiertes', so this page opens 'Mono- oder Dialkylamino, ...'. Printed line breaks are not preserved here; the two words split across a line at a hyphen ('N-Alkyl-N-' / 'heteroarylamino' and 'N-Alkyl-N-' / 'heteroarylaminosulfonyl') are rejoined without a space. Two gaps in the otherwise regular series are as printed and must not be filled in: the amino series jumps from 'Cycloalkenylamino' straight to 'Heterocyclylalkylamino' with no 'Heterocyclylamino', and the sulfonylamino series jumps from 'Cycloalkylalkinylsulfonylamino' to 'Cycloalkenylalkylsulfonylamino' with no 'Cycloalkenylsulfonylamino'. A small stray ink speck sits above the line ending 'N-Alkyl-N-' (fourth printed line), to the right of 'Cycloalkenylamino' on the line below; it is scanning dirt, not a character. The en field is a literal rendering of the same list: the German nouns are chemical group names, so only the connective words ('gegebenenfalls substituiertes' -> 'optionally substituted', 'oder' -> 'or') and the German 'Alkinyl' -> English 'alkynyl' actually change.
